builders.angle: LITERAL -- work BRIEF-r39's fix list 1 to 3 in order and exactly as written, one wing at a time, the Bathhouse FIRST (the round's fight and the lowest of the four, 4 from judge 2). Keep every change inside your four wings.

THE NEAR FLOOR FIRST -- the angle that won rounds 31, 35 and 37. Carry the nearFloor rule as rounds 34-37 extended it into all four wings -- a dressed, lit near floor with a light pool from a source the room has and objects standing IN it above the hand's edge -- prove it there, then each wing's own defect in that light.

THE OBJECT DRAWN, NOT A PRIMITIVE. Each wing's subject is a weak object: the Bathhouse's tiny tubs, the Lampworks' stick benches, the Kitchens' blank polygon flags, the Ballroom's rectangle-grid wall. Draw each as a real object with an inked, broken silhouette and mass first -- clawfoot tubs with rims and water, benches loaded with glass and tools, worn chipped flags, carved damask panels -- then bring it forward into the light.
